newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Corps closes more locks on upper Mississippi.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Corps closes more locks on upper Mississippi.

text.p: High water prompted the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers to close two more locks on the upper Mississippi, a spokeswoman said Tuesday.
"We did close Lock No. 3 in addition to Lock No. 4," said Mari K. Cronberg, spokeswoman for the Corp's St. Paul District.
The additional closures mean the river is shut to navigation from Upper and Lower St. Anthony's Falls north of Minneapolis, Minn. to Alma, Wisc.
"There's high water elevation, and when it gets that high, the river runs extremely fast," Cronberg said. "It's basically for safety purposes."
Melting snow and rain is forecast to push the Mississippi to levels that are the highest in 28 years, Cronberg said.
Flooding and snowstorms in Minnesota and the Dakotas have disrupted rail movement, caused massive power outages and prompted people to evacuate their homes.
The Mississippi River at Minneapolis is currently at 16.1 feet and is forecast to crest at 20 feet on April 11, Cronberg said.
